A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tree-Guided Diffusion Planner and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K. Corresponding scientific content can be reliably matched throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Maze2D, KUKA manipulation, and AntMaze experiments in Tables 1–3, plus timing, sensitivity, ablation, and additional benchmark results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and supplementary analyses in Appendices G–K.

M1.justification: State decomposition, particle-guided parent branching, conditional subtree expansion, trajectory selection, and action execution are unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 and the pipeline in Appendix A retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Maze2D gold-picking scenarios, KUKA PNP and PNWP tasks, AntMaze multi-goal exploration, and standard pointmaze/antmaze benchmarks in Appendix J. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding tables: Diffuser, Diffuserγ/TAT, MCSS, MCSS+SS, and AdaptDiffuser where applicable. Citation renumbering does not introduce different comparison methods.

E3.justification: The task configurations, sampling budgets, planning horizons, diffusion steps, guidance settings, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Table 4 and Appendix F retain the same settings and scoring procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablations, trajectory-diversity analysis in Figure 5, timing analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, sample-budget ablations, and learned-versus-fixed particle-guidance comparison. Their questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report five seeds per Maze2D task, 100 seeds for the main KUKA and AntMaze comparisons, and the same standard-error reporting. No repeated-run information or statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, TDP's Table 1 single-task and multi-task averages remain 43.7 and 72.4, and Appendix J's antmaze-giant result remains 98 ± 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, Proposition 1 and its assumptions, and the proof in Appendix C are mathematically unchanged. Differences concern punctuation, spacing, and equation-reference wording.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, zero-shot planning through bi-level trajectory sampling and improved performance on challenging test-time objectives. Copyediting does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of exploration, local optima, conditional versus unconditional particle guidance, and component contributions remain unchanged. Both versions acknowledge computational overhead and propose more efficient search or learned priors as future work.

D1.justification: The algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameter disclosures, RTX 3090 hardware information, planning-time measurements, and project-page link remain the same. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: All 52 cited works match across versions, and their substantive use and research positioning are unchanged. v2 reorders references and updates publication metadata; these are bibliographic presentation edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, punctuation, and sentence-flow edits throughout the main text, standardizes some cross-references, and reformats bibliography entries. It also adds funding acknowledgements and replaces the preprint footer with the NeurIPS 2025 conference designation; the scientific section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–14 retain their content and display structure. Small layout changes include text reflow, the conference footer, and acknowledgements above the reordered and reformatted references.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability through sentence splitting in the abstract and grammatical corrections such as replacing 'enables to discover' in Section 5.2. Fuller publication details and funding acknowledgements improve documentation. The method, theory, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to editorial polish and disclosure.
